engagement_title: Halcyon Grid before the conference: rebuild three AI-generated marks into a production vector family, bring eleven self-submitted headshots to one credible look, rebuild the printer's exhibitor card into a live run, and hand back the mark sheet editable
vertical: Technology & SaaS (eleven-person seed-stage company selling scheduling infrastructure to logistics operations teams, Denver, Colorado)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork brief in which the client's logo had been 'created on AI' and needed turning into a 'vector file so it can be used in multiple platforms', kept 'high-quality across different formats'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com open call 'Vectorize Logos & Packaging', where the client already has 'AI-generated artwork ... but it is still in raster form and not ready for production' and needs 'everything redrawn as clean, fully-editable vectors so I can scale them for any application without loss of quality', with scope including preserving 'every colour, gradient, and detail exactly as in the original concept while improving line sharpness and overall balance'. Both are laundered to a fictional seed-stage company, Halcyon Grid; no real company, product, person, trademark or AI tool is named in any task-facing field. The ledger verdict was REBUILD, because as banked it sat on one surface: three traces, done. The second anchor's own wording is also a trap the connector will not honour, since a trace of a gradient returns dozens of near-identical flat fills, so the honest commission is a reduction argued and defended rather than exact preservation promised. VECTOR-09 restores what these clients needed: a mark family that has to hold together, a printed run in flight against a conference date, and a sheet somebody else can work from.
client_one_liner: Eleven people, six weeks to a developer conference, three logos our founder generated at two in the morning, and a printer who has already told us he cannot use what we sent him.
client_brief:
Halcyon Grid: turn what our founder made into a real brand system before the conference.

We are eleven people building scheduling infrastructure for logistics teams. Seats are twenty to sixty dollars a month and the people who sign are engineers and operations leads.

Two years ago our founder made our logo in an AI tool at two in the morning, and made two more the same way for the sub products. They have been good enough for a website and they are not good enough for anything else. All we have are the exports, and they are soft at the edges. Our printer has told us he cannot use them. So has the app store listing.

So, first: rebuild the three marks as proper artwork we can hand to anybody. A printer, a fabricator, an app store, a partner's marketing team. They should scale up to a banner and down to a browser tab without changing character. The two sub product marks were made separately and they have never felt like they belong to the same family as the main one, and they should. Our founder is attached to the gradient on the main mark, so tell us honestly what happens to it.

We need the marks to exist as a system, not three files: the name set beside the mark horizontally and stacked, an app icon, a favicon, a one-ink version, a reversed version for dark backgrounds, and a sheet that tells someone which one to use where. Keep that sheet editable, because we will be adding a fourth product this year.

Second: the exhibitor cards. We are at a developer conference in six weeks. Our printer holds last year's card file and we do not. Keep the card, put this year's eleven people on it with their own photographs, and make each card point people at that person's own booking link the way last year's did. Send back something the printer can run plus one file per person, named to them.

On look: our buyers are technical and they read fuss as sloppiness. Sharp, plain, restrained. If something in our own list turns out to be a bad idea, tell us before you build it.
price_band_and_audience: Seats 20 to 60 dollars per user per month, sold to engineering and operations leads at mid-sized logistics firms, decided by a technical evaluator rather than a brand buyer. The band is load-bearing: this audience reads pixel-crisp geometric restraint as engineering credibility and reads gloss, glow and decorative detail as a company that spends on appearance rather than reliability, so the correct answer is a reduction toward sharp minimal geometry with quiet type, and a mark sheet that reads as documentation rather than marketing. A consumer lifestyle app at the same price would take the opposite answer and it would be wrong here. An agent that preserves the founder's glow because the founder is attached to it, without arguing the case, has ducked the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A seed-stage software company selling scheduling infrastructure to logistics operations teams, with a main product and two sub-products.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024, Denver, Colorado. Eleven people, six weeks out from their first developer conference.
brand_identity.about: Halcyon Grid builds scheduling infrastructure for logistics operations teams, sold by the seat to the engineers and operations leads who run the floor. The product is judged on reliability, and the brand is meant to say the same thing the software does: precise, plain, and built to be depended on.
brand_identity.audience: Engineering and operations leads at mid-sized logistics firms, decided by a technical evaluator rather than a brand buyer. An audience that reads fuss as sloppiness and crispness as competence.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Seats 20 to 60 dollars per user per month. Mid-market infrastructure pricing, sold on reliability and evaluation rather than on brand aspiration. The visual language reads as engineering credibility, never as marketing spend.
brand_identity.typography: Wordmark and headings in a geometric grotesque with tight, even weight and no decorative detail. Body and documentation in a clean neutral sans with strong numerals. Type is set to read as documentation, not as a campaign.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, unadorned, engineer to engineer. No hype, no gloss. Example line: "Sharp, plain, restrained. If something in our own list turns out to be a bad idea, tell us before you build it."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The three marks (the main mark and two sub-product marks) were generated by the founder in an AI tool two years ago, on separate nights with different settings. Only the soft-edged raster exports survive, with no source files. They go soft as soon as anyone scales them, and the printer and the app store listing have both said they cannot use them. No production vector artwork exists.
brand_identity.values: Reliability and restraint. Geometry over decoration, documentation over marketing. Say honestly what the artwork can and cannot do, including the founder's gradient.

assets_supplied.name: halcyon_master_mark.png (1400 x 1400)
assets_supplied.kind: The primary mark as exported from a generative image tool: an angular interlocking figure with a soft outer glow, filled with a blue to violet gradient, on transparency.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our main mark. This export is everything we have of it. It goes soft as soon as anybody scales it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The figure's two supposedly matching arms were never drawn to match: the generator produced them freehand, so their widths and corner angles differ, which the soft edges of a 1400 pixel export hide completely and which becomes legible only once the shape is real geometry seen large. And the outer glow is part of the artwork rather than a background, so any preparation separating artwork from ground by lightness carries a fringe of it through as a ring of stray shapes.

assets_supplied.name: subbrand_marks/ (2 PNGs, 1024 x 1024 and 1600 x 1600)
assets_supplied.kind: The two sub-product marks, generated separately several months apart with different settings.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The two sub product marks. They were made at different times and they have never quite matched the main one."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. One sits on transparency and the other was flattened onto a plate whose white is a very light warm grey, so the preparation that isolates one correctly returns the substrate on the other and the failure looks like a plausible mask either way. And one of the two is built around an enclosed ring, so the one-call knockout route returns a solid opaque disc with the plate still inside it while reporting success.

assets_supplied.name: exhibitor_card_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for last year's exhibitor card, from a real page layout with embedded font subsets, one card per page, 89 x 51 mm.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our printer ran last year. Nobody here has the working file. Keep the card."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two structural facts nothing announces. The name, role, product line, email and booking link came across as one continuous story rather than five addressable frames, and the mapping readout silently omits one of those runs, so every offset past it is short while the validator still reports the mapping valid and the prepare call still reports the placeholders created. And the card's code block converts to an ordinary graphic frame that accepts a per-record code mapping, validates it and reports it created, while no code is ever produced on any rendered page.

assets_supplied.name: team_roster.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The HR sheet export, one row per person: name, role, product line, email, booking link, photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This year's eleven. The product line column is which of the three things each person owns."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The photo column keys on surname and two people share one, so two rows bind the same photograph while every filename resolves. And one row's product line names a fourth product announced internally that has no mark in the supplied artwork, so that card carries a field the mark set cannot answer.

assets_supplied.name: team_photos/ (11 self-submitted frames, 1200 to 4000 px)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs the eleven people sent in themselves, taken on phones in offices, at home and outdoors, with no common direction.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everyone sent in whatever they had. They are all recognisable, which is mostly what matters."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Two were shot against bright office windows, so the sitter's shoulder and the blown window share luminance and a subject knockout returns success while quietly eating the shoulder line. And one is a 1200 pixel copy pulled off a profile page rather than an original, so it binds and resolves like the rest and simply prints soft at card trim, where no route can put back detail the original export already discarded.

assets_supplied.name: halcyon_booth_code.png
assets_supplied.kind: A single scannable code image the company generated from its own booking system, pointing at the shared booth page.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The code for our booth page. We made this one ourselves."

assets_supplied.name: founder_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from the founder about what the mark is meant to mean and what she likes about it, with no hex values and no measurements.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What she was going for. Read it, then tell us what you think."

acceptance_bar: Each mark comes back as artwork we can hand to a printer, a fabricator or an app store: placeable, scalable, transparent, with nothing behind it and no box appearing on a dark background.
The three marks read as one family laid out together at one size, matched on weight, corner treatment and proportion, not merely filed together.
Enclosed shapes stay enclosed. A ring that has filled in or a counter that has closed is a rejected file.
No mark carries stray fragments, halo shapes or leftover edge debris from what was around it in the original export.
A version claimed as one ink is genuinely one ink, not a family of near-identical inks.
The mark still reads as our mark at browser-tab size and at banner size, and the small versions are not simply the large one made smaller if that does not work.

The eleven photographs read as one set when the cards are laid out in a row: one white point, one warmth, one black point, one crop logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named to us rather than shipped at eighty percent.
No file is larger than the frame it came from, and nothing is cut out sloppily. A bitten shoulder or a chewed hairline is rejected on sight, and the note lists every picture resized and by how much.

Exhibitor cards: one page per person in roster order, every line last year's card carried present on every page, the photograph on each card the person named on it, at real print resolution at 89 x 51 mm trim.
One card file per person, named to them, and its contents are what its name claims.

The mark sheet is one working file we can edit ourselves, every canvas at its own size, every mark as real artwork and the words as live text, plus the source it was built from, in one type system whose family, foundry and weight you name per role, stating plainly that the wordmark type is a face you chose rather than the one the generator drew.

A written note: what happened to the gradient and why, what was done to each photograph, anything in our own list you questioned, and anything you could not do inside the printer's file, told to us before it reaches the printer.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize, counted here and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, masked and unmasked image_apply_adjustments, image_apply_auto_tone, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, image_remove_background on both routes, image_auto_straighten, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every reduction and portrait decision. Three generative rasters made months apart need three different preparations before anything is traced, and the tracing call takes no options at all, so raster preparation is the only lever over what the artwork becomes. The same surface brings eleven self-submitted phone photographs to one credible house treatment and cuts them to the card crop without upscaling anything.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml twice (to read the conversion, then to audit the prepared template), generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and recordRange, document_render_layout at resolution 300 with createSeparateFiles and pageRange in N-N form
adobe_surfaces.role: The printed half: the printer's flat card becomes a live merge template with no working file to start from, the roster becomes the data source, and the run yields the press file, eleven per-person named cards and 300 ppi proofs. The only surface that does record per page, and where a request the client made in good faith must be answered against what the tooling can actually carry.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html for transport, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The mark sheet: a documentation page, an icon and favicon board, a lockup page and a dark booth panel in one export, each root carrying its own canvas size, native and editable with live text and every mark as real vector shapes. This is where the three marks are finally adjacent at one size in one document.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per role, font_styles for numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts to launder names into canonical PostScript form, get_fontkit_embed_url for one kit consumed through the returned kebab css_stack
adobe_surfaces.role: The wordmark lockups and the sheet. Nothing in the connector reads a typeface off a picture, so the face beside the mark is chosen art direction that must be disclosed as chosen, and the recommender refuses to pair. Numeric weight is non-standard per family, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one unresolvable name kills the entire kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed operations frame for the booth panel, which an eleven-person company cannot shoot before the conference and which is the only IP-clean way to introduce a photograph nobody there took, plus the selects board the founder and printer sign off from before the press file is committed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook before writing markup, settle which half of the commission lands on which surface, and upload every asset through initialize, PUT and finalize.
trajectory.judgement: The split is the first real decision and the brief never states it. Exhibitor cards are record per page against artwork the client wants preserved; the mark sheet needs several canvas sizes and must stay editable when a fourth product lands.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming surface per deliverable, the confirmed tier, and a manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at all three marks at full size and triage them: what each is made of, what is artwork and what is glow, what each sits on, and where each encloses negative space.
trajectory.judgement: These look like three versions of one problem and they are not. A mark on transparency, a mark flattened onto an off-white plate and a mark built around an enclosed ring need three different preparations, and choosing one route for the folder is the failure.
trajectory.produces: A per-mark triage note covering ground, enclosure and what belongs to the artwork.

trajectory.action: Prepare and trace each mark by its own route: ink-level selections worded against the artwork's visual properties rather than its substrate, the correct polarity, crops to the selection's bounds, trace, then inject a viewBox, strip the opaque full-canvas path, clear stray glow fragments and build the one-ink and reversed colourways.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions per mark the tools do not make: wording, polarity, and whether to trace the binary plate or the colour-accurate plate. The colour route is where the founder's gradient question gets its real answer, since a trace of a gradient is not a gradient. A mark surrounded by halo debris is not production artwork whatever it looks like at thumbnail size.
trajectory.produces: Three cleaned marks with on-light, on-dark and one-ink colourways, route and polarity recorded per mark.

trajectory.action: Place the master mark large and then at browser-tab size, and look at the geometry as geometry rather than as a picture.
trajectory.judgement: The first moment the artwork is real rather than soft, and the first moment its construction can be judged at all. The agent must be willing to conclude that the client's own mark is not built the way the client believes, and decide whether that is reportable, correctable by a different preparation, or outside scope.
trajectory.produces: A written finding on the master mark's construction at both extremes of size.

trajectory.action: Derive the icon, favicon and lockup-scale artwork from the cleaned masters, reading the confidence and tradeoff metadata each crop returns rather than trusting success.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoff array is the only signal that a crop clipped, that a detection was weak, or that an output was interpolated upward toward the cap. A favicon made by shrinking a mark never designed to shrink is a decision rather than an export.
trajectory.produces: Icon and favicon artwork with a no-enlargement record drawn from what each call reported.

trajectory.action: Triage the eleven photographs on light, level, sitter tightness, true source scale and isolation risk, then level what needs it and bring every frame toward one house treatment with its own parameter set, masking where a whole-frame grade would blow a window or grey a skin tone.
trajectory.judgement: Self-submitted portraits are eleven separate problems wearing one folder name, and one batched call would apply one identical parameter set to all eleven. Prompt wording is the whole gate on the masks.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note and eleven graded portraits at their true source scale with a parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut each portrait to the card crop, choosing the isolation route per frame, and inspect each edge at card reproduction size rather than at full frame.
trajectory.judgement: A subject knockout is right where the sitter separates from the ground and wrong where a shoulder and a blown window share luminance, and the wrong route returns success. Route is a per-frame decision made by looking.
trajectory.produces: Eleven card-crop portraits with the route recorded per frame.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster against the photographs and the mark set, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with an image column of bare filenames under the required prefix, upload the graded card masters and build the image map against them.
trajectory.judgement: A photo column keyed on surname is fine until two people share one, and a product line with no artwork behind it is a question for the client rather than a field to leave blank. The client asked to be told, so resolving either silently is not the same act as resolving it and saying so.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded masters, the image map, and a first list of questions for the handover.

trajectory.action: Convert the card PDF, export IDML, unzip it, and read what came across: frame counts, object styles, real integer page-item ids and bounds, and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided here and the answer is a property of the client's PDF, not of the plan. There must be a real addressable frame for everything already promised, since the whole per-row binding depends on there being a frame to bind to.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping against what the conversion exposed, including the per-record binding the card's code block appears to offer, validate it, prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this verification and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with per-row images bound, render the press file and proofs at 300 ppi, then produce the per-person single-page files and name each to its person, verifying identity by opening each file rather than by its position in the returned list.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to PDF forfeits the per-record branch. Naming eleven files by return order is the fast wrong answer, and it is the failure somebody discovers at a booth.
trajectory.produces: The press card file, 300 ppi proofs, and eleven identity-verified named single cards.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the booth panel frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house treatment and lay it beside the portrait set.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose light can be brought to the house treatment rather than the prettiest thumbnail, and a subject a technical audience will not read as stock filler. Both are cheap to get wrong at 240 pixels.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame, graded, judged in or out with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Fonts and Adobe Express, HTML authoring
trajectory.action: Build one kit (recommend per role, pull style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name), then author one self-contained HTML with four roots at four canvas sizes, base64-inline every photograph, place every mark as inline vector in an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check and export. Verify through both channels: resolve the rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Nothing here reads the face the generator drew, so the wordmark type is the agent's own choice and must be presented as a choice; numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name and one unresolvable name kills the kit. In the export, a URL photograph is not a photograph, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, a right-anchored auto-sized wrapper collapses off the artboard, and every drop returns success while the preview shows only the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry and numeric weight per role plus the chosen-face disclosure, a native editable Express document holding every canvas, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the graded portrait set, the licensed frame and the card proofs within the per-call cap, treating a partial success as partial and re-sending only the entries named as failed. Then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The founder asked to be told honestly about her gradient, the roster raised a question the mark set cannot answer, and the card carries a request that must be met differently from how it was asked. All three belong in writing before the printer sees anything.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover the acceptance bar requires.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What is actually inside these three generative exports, legible only once they are real geometry. The master's two supposedly matching arms were drawn freehand and differ in width and corner angle, which a 1400 pixel soft-edged export hides completely; at trace, seen large, the mark is visibly lopsided. The outer glow belongs to the artwork rather than a background, so a preparation that separates by lightness carries a fringe through as a ring of stray shapes. And the two sub-brand marks, made months apart, come back with materially different stroke mass from each other and from the master even where every preparation succeeded. Nothing reports any of it: every selection returns a plausible mask, the tracer takes no options, and each mark inspected alone at thumbnail size looks finished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no parameter to reason about and no read-ahead: the tracer has no options, so the only way to learn what a preparation yields is to make it, trace it and look at it large. Nothing states it, since the brief says only that the exports are soft and that the sub marks have never felt like family, the client's complaint rather than a description of the geometry. And the response is not a re-run but a different preparation per mark, a decision about whether a construction fault in the client's own mark is correctable here or reportable, and usually a change to which mark carries which application.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare each mark on a different route, a selection worded for the structural edge rather than the luminous field, or the colour-plate route instead of the binary route, then re-trace, re-strip the opaque path, re-clear the halo debris and re-place large and at tab size. Decide explicitly what to do about the asymmetry and the gradient, since neither can be redrawn here, and re-take the icon and favicon derivation, because a mark that only holds above a certain size needs different small artwork rather than a smaller copy.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A brand system shipped to a printer, a fabricator and an app store in which the company's primary mark is visibly lopsided at every size it is now sharp enough to show it, ringed by halo fragments, with two sub marks that still do not belong to it, delivered as the production-clean artwork the client paid for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card exposes and what it will actually carry. The name, role, product line, email and booking link came across as one continuous story rather than five addressable frames, and the mapping readout omits one of those runs, so every offset computed past it is short while the validator reports the mapping valid, the prepare call reports the placeholders created successfully, and only some of the fields land. And the card's code block converts to an ordinary graphic frame that accepts a per-record code mapping, passes validation and is reported created, while no code is ever produced on any rendered page. The client asked in good faith for each card to point at that person's own link, because last year's card did.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity is a property of a document made by a printer nobody has spoken to, and the code binding is documented and accepted by every tool in the chain right up to the render, so no ordering and no amount of care reaches either fact earlier. Nothing states it: the brief states the goal, that each card points at that person's own booking link, a client requirement rather than a description of what the tooling will do. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping changes shape to offset arithmetic against an independently reconstructed story, and the per-person code must be re-planned into a different deliverable.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story from the IDML content runs, recompute every offset from that string, re-validate, re-prepare and re-verify by grepping the round-tripped IDML for every placeholder before any page is merged. Then take the code decision explicitly: bind the single booth code the client already supplied to every card and set each person's own link as live text, or ask the client for eleven exported code images so they bind through the per-row image column, and say in writing which was done and why.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press run of eleven exhibitor cards on which the booking link is silently missing from every card and the code block is last year's flat placeholder pointing nowhere, handed to a printer six weeks before a conference, with every tool having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame belongs with this set, a question that exists only once the two are adjacent. Stock search returns a 240 pixel thumbnail and true dimensions and says nothing about the light, so the frame's real colour temperature, contrast and grain arrive only with the full-resolution download, and the comparison it must survive is against eleven phone portraits just pulled to one house treatment. A frame that looked crisp and neutral as a thumbnail can land warm, soft and evidently lit by somebody else, and the failure is not that it is a bad photograph but that it reads as bought the moment it sits beside the team.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The judgement requires both halves to exist and the graded portrait set is the second half, so ordering cannot bring it forward. Care cannot dodge it either, because nothing in the search response describes the light and the thumbnail is too small to read it. Nothing states it: the brief never mentions a photograph at all, and the panel is the agent's own proposal. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different frame, a materially harder grade, or a panel re-composed around type and the marks.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay the downloaded frame beside the graded portraits at panel size and judge it there rather than alone. Then either search again on the light rather than the subject and license a replacement, or push this frame with masked corrections until it sits with the set, or drop it and re-author the booth panel without a photograph, which changes the panel's composition, its type hierarchy and which mark variant carries it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A booth panel standing next to eleven cards at a developer conference in which the hero photograph is visibly lit by a different person on a different day in a different colour from every face beside it, in front of the exact audience the brief says reads fuss as sloppiness.

deliverables.name: Halcyon Grid production mark family
deliverables.spec: Three marks rebuilt from generative rasters as placeable, scalable artwork with real viewBoxes, no opaque ground paths, no halo debris and enclosed shapes genuinely enclosed, in on-light, on-dark and one-ink colourways, plus horizontal and stacked wordmark lockups, an app icon and a favicon. The three must hold together as one family laid out at one size, with the preparation route recorded per mark and the gradient decision argued rather than asserted.

deliverables.name: Exhibitor cards, press file plus per-person named cards
deliverables.spec: 89 x 51 mm, one person per card in roster order, page count equal to roster count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim, binding name, role, product line, email and booking link verbatim from the roster plus that person's own photograph. With one single-page file per person, named to them and identity-verified by opening it, and 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, handed back with a record of how it was derived and of what the card could not be made to carry.

deliverables.name: Team portrait set at one house treatment

decision_gates: The surface split: exhibitor cards to the merge surface because they are record per page against artwork the client wants preserved, mark sheet to HTML authoring because it needs several canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Whether three superficially similar generative exports are one problem or three, when one sits on transparency, one on an off-white plate and one encloses a ring.
Selection wording per mark: whether the prompt takes the artwork or the plate it was flattened onto.
Which polarity to hand a tracer that takes no options, and whether to trace the binary plate or the colour-accurate plate.
What honestly happens to the founder's gradient, and whether to say so or to quietly ship whatever the trace returned.
Whether a construction fault in the client's own mark is correctable inside this engagement, reportable, or both.
Whether to strip the opaque ground path and clear the halo debris, which nothing in the chain does and nothing warns about.
Isolation route per portrait, when a subject knockout is right against a plain wall and wrong against a blown window.

Whether to bind the client's own surname-keyed photo references or rebuild the image map against the agent's graded masters, and whether repointing a client's data silently is the same act as repointing it and saying so.
What to do with a roster row naming a product the mark set cannot answer.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification, when nothing instructs a re-export and grep of the prepared template.
How to answer a per-record request the client made in good faith once it is clear the chain reports it done and produces nothing.
Whether to name eleven per-person card files by the order they came back or by opening each one.
Whether the licensed frame joins the set or reads as bought, and if bought, whether to push it, replace it or compose the panel without it.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these assets into a frontier image model and it returns three nice logos. It fails all three gates. IDENTITY: the commission is that these three specific marks, which the founder made and the company has used for two years, must survive being rebuilt rather than be replaced; a regenerated mark is a different company's logo, and the printer, the fabricator and the app store listing all receive it. The eleven faces are eleven real colleagues standing at a booth, not eleven plausible portraits. SPEC: one card per person in roster order at 89 x 51 mm and 300 ppi with five named fields bound verbatim from their own roster, eleven separately named card files each containing the person their filename claims, artwork with real viewBoxes and no opaque ground paths, and no delivered file larger than its true source. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked against a roster. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next year is a data change, and a native document with live text and real vector so a fourth product can be added without a re-commission. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: is this arm the same as that one, does this placeholder exist, does this code ever appear, is this face the person named beside it.
doability_proof: All verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account); five surfaces, honestly counted, with image_vectorize in the Photoshop family rather than as an Illustrator surface. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template producing a story containing the expected placeholders). One record per page is confirmed for PDF output; per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore never used for identity; true 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is silently ignored. THE CARD PDF IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE: a PDF with two placed image blocks converts to an .indd exposing two graphic frames plus split text frames, and a contiguous copy flow collapses into a single story, which is exactly a portrait plus a code block with a five-line copy column beside them; it must be a real font-embedding press PDF from a full engine, since a thin hand-authored PDF fails conversion opaquely. THE VARIABLE CODE IS A VERIFIED FALSE POSITIVE, NOT AN INVENTION: qr_mappings was tested twice, alone and alongside an image merge, and in both cases the validator accepted it, prepare_indd_merge_template returned success, and the rendered page still showed the original flat placeholder with the round-tripped IDML carrying zero code markers. The task never requires a variable code to be produced; it requires the request to be answered, and the client-supplied single code image binds through the ordinary image route. The lossy textContent readout and the validator returning VALID on the resulting wrong offsets are likewise verified. Per-row image merge through an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified; eleven rows here, so the recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, masked apply_adjustments, auto_tone, auto_straighten, remove_background on both routes and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, as are the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the enclosed-aperture failure of remove_background returning a solid opaque disc while reporting success, the binary mask, the mandatory polarity flip before tracing, vectorize taking no options at all, its missing viewBox and opaque path zero, its dozens of near-identical fills from a colour plate, and its explosion into loose ungrouped shapes in Express. Upscaling is handled not asserted: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap and signals it only in metadata.tradeoffs, which makes the 1200 pixel web-copy portrait a scored decision. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, and the right-anchored auto-sized wrapper collapse is a verified defect; transport is pinned to the upload route with media_type text/html; verification is split because the rendition preview shows page one only; persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the document plus the source HTML. FONTS: the chain is verified end to end, no font identification from an image exists anywhere in the connector (which is why the wordmark face must be disclosed as chosen), and the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule and the all-or-nothing kit call are live findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, the orientation filter is broken and never used, the 240 pixel rendition is not editable which is what makes the frame's true light a download-time discovery, licensed downloads are genuine camera scale, and board placements cap at twelve per call with failedItems signalling partial success. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no document_render_vector or document_merge_data_vector, no bleed, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above twenty files.
